name: Cervical Myelopathy
summary: Cervical myelopathy means the spinal cord in the neck is under pressure or has been injured. The most common cause in adults is degenerative narrowing of the spinal canal (disc bulges, bony spurs, thickened ligaments).

looksLike: Clumsy or numb hands (trouble with buttons, writing, dropping things).
Unsteady, stiff or wide-based walking; feeling that the legs are heavy.
Symptoms in both hands or both legs, though one side may be worse.
Neck stiffness; electric-shock feeling down the spine on neck flexion (Lhermitte sign).
Later features: bladder urgency or incontinence, bowel change.
Neck pain may be mild or absent. Do not rely on pain.
redFlags: Rapidly worsening weakness, gait or hand function
Bladder or bowel change with new limb signs
Acute neck trauma plus neurological signs
Stable but clear UMN signs with no rapid change
firstSteps: Initial approach: recognise, document, refer. No neck loading.
Justifying findings: UMN signs, hand and gait change.
Priority: safe referral at the right urgency.

assess: Observe gait: stiff, wide-based or unsteady steps.
Tandem walk (heel to toe) and Romberg test (standing with feet together, then eyes closed).
Hand function: grip, finger movement, grip-and-release test.
Full neurological screen: dermatomes, myotomes, reflexes in all four limbs.
Upper motor neuron (UMN) signs: Hoffmann, inverted supinator, clonus, Babinski.
Gentle cervical range only if safe. Do not apply end-range loading, compression or traction.

differentials: Normal pressure hydrocephalus or Parkinson's disease

tests.name: Hoffmann sign
tests.purpose: Screen for UMN involvement in the upper limb
tests.positive: Involuntary flexion of the thumb and index finger
tests.patientPosition: Sitting, hand relaxed with the fingers slightly flexed
tests.therapistPosition: In front, holding the patient's middle finger
procedure: Hold the middle finger at the middle phalanx. Quickly flick the fingernail of the middle finger downward so the fingertip snaps
tests.interpretation: UMN pathway involvement; supports further assessment If positive, complete the rest of the UMN screen and consider referral

tests.name: Babinski sign
tests.purpose: Screen for UMN involvement in the lower limb
tests.positive: Great toe extends (goes up), other toes may fan
procedure: Stroke firmly along the outer edge of the sole from the heel toward the toes, then curve across the ball of the foot

tests.name: Inverted supinator sign
tests.positive: Finger flexion with little or no forearm movement; sometimes with shoulder flexion
procedure: Tap the brachioradialis tendon at the distal radius
tests.interpretation: Suggests a lesion at the C5–C6 level with UMN involvement. Interpret within the cluster

tests.name: Ankle clonus
tests.positive: Rhythmic repeated beats of the foot
procedure: Support the knee slightly flexed; quickly dorsiflex the ankle and hold light pressure

tests.name: Grip-and-release test
tests.positive: Slow or incomplete cycles compared with normal reference values
procedure: The patient makes a fist and opens it fully, as fast as possible, for 10 seconds, with the arm held in front

blocks.text: **Cervical myelopathy** means the spinal cord in the neck is under pressure or has been injured. The most common cause in adults is degenerative narrowing of the spinal canal (disc bulges, bony spurs, thickened ligaments) [Ref – to verify]. The spinal cord carries signals between the brain and the body, so cord compromise causes problems in the hands, legs, balance and sometimes bladder control, not just neck pain.

**Why physiotherapists must know this chapter:** myelopathy is often missed because it develops slowly and mimics ageing, carpal tunnel syndrome or clumsiness. Missing it can delay surgical review. Your main job is to recognise it and refer safely.

items: Clumsy or numb hands (trouble with buttons, writing, dropping things).
Unsteady, stiff or wide-based walking; feeling that the legs are heavy.
Symptoms in both hands or both legs, though one side may be worse.
Neck stiffness; electric-shock feeling down the spine on neck flexion (Lhermitte sign).
Later features: bladder urgency or incontinence, bowel change.
Neck pain may be mild or absent. Do not rely on pain.

blocks.text: **Common findings versus findings that strongly suggest another diagnosis:** hand clumsiness with gait change points to myelopathy. A single-arm pain pattern with normal gait points more toward radiculopathy (Vol 2 Ch 1).

rows: Have your hands become clumsy, for example buttons or handwriting?
Hand function loss suggests cord involvement
Has your walking changed? Do you feel unsteady in the dark?
Are both hands or both legs affected?
Any electric shocks down your back when you bend your neck?
Any change in bladder or bowel control?
How fast has it changed over weeks or months?
Any trauma, fever, weight loss, cancer history?

blocks.text: Combining

A published clinical prediction cluster for myelopathy includes gait deviation, a positive Hoffmann sign, an inverted supinator sign, a positive Babinski sign and age above 45 [Ref – to verify exact criteria and likelihood ratios before teaching as a rule]. A greater number of positive items raises the likelihood of myelopathy. A negative screen does not rule it out. The deciding tool is MRI, requested by a physician.

rows: Arm pain in a root pattern, normal gait, no UMN signs
Hand tingling mainly at night, normal gait
Stocking-glove numbness, reduced ankle reflexes, no UMN signs
Younger patient, relapsing episodes, vision problems
Weakness and wasting without sensory loss
Numb feet and hands, memory or mood change
Constant pain, night pain, fever, weight loss
Normal pressure hydrocephalus or Parkinson's disease
Gait change with other brain-related features

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Rapidly worsening weakness, gait or hand function
Stop the session, document, arrange transfer to emergency or spine service
Bladder or bowel change with new limb signs
Acute neck trauma plus neurological signs
Stable but clear UMN signs with no rapid change
Compression likely but not rapidly worsening
Stop neck loading, refer to spine surgeon or neurologist

blocks.text: **Stop or defer:** cervical manipulation, traction, compression tests, end-range positions.

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency red flag? **Yes:** emergency action.
Hand clumsiness, gait change, or UMN signs? **Yes:** working diagnosis is suspected cervical myelopathy. Go to step 3.
Is the change rapid? **Yes:** urgent same-day review. **No:** urgent referral within days.
Document findings (gait, hand function, reflexes, UMN signs) so the physician sees the baseline.

blocks.text: **Supports:** hand clumsiness, bilateral signs, gait change, Hoffmann, Babinski, hyperreflexia. **Argues against:** purely unilateral radicular pattern with normal gait and reflexes. **Must not miss:** progressive compression, tumour, infection.

**Preferred starting choice: none to the neck.** Do not apply cervical manipulation, traction, strong mobilization or end-range techniques while cord compression is suspected. The risk may outweigh any benefit [Ref – to verify]. Gentle thoracic and shoulder girdle work may be considered only after medical clearance and when it does not provoke cord symptoms.
Before medical assessment, do not start a strengthening program. After physician review:

rows: Mild stable myelopathy managed non-surgically by the medical team
Supervised program agreed with the team: gait and balance training, hand dexterity, gentle general conditioning, fall-prevention advice. Avoid end-range neck loading
Follow the surgeon's protocol: early walking, gradual range, hand and gait retraining, progressive strengthening as cleared

blocks.text: Example progression logic: if gait stays stable and no new symptoms appear for the review period, increase walking time and balance difficulty gradually. If any new weakness, hand deterioration or bladder change appears, stop and refer. These are illustrations, not a protocol.
Not indicated as a primary treatment. They do not change cord compression. If the patient is awaiting review, avoid heat or electrical applications that mask worsening sensory change.

items: Recognise and document.
Refer using the urgency level from Section G.
Educate: explain that the neck needs medical imaging, avoid risky activities and falls, report any sudden worsening.
After medical decision: support conservative care or post-operative rehabilitation.

blocks.text: Track: gait (tandem walk, 10-metre walk time), hand function (grip-and-release), strength, reflexes, bladder status, and a validated myelopathy outcome such as the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale where available [Ref – to verify]. Worsening on any item means urgent referral.

**Case:** A 63-year-old man reports six months of dropping things and walking unsteadily. Both hands are numb. Hoffmann sign is positive bilaterally, gait is wide-based, and reflexes in the legs are brisk. He has no bladder change.

**Working diagnosis:** suspected cervical myelopathy. **Action:** urgent referral to a spine surgeon or neurologist for imaging. No cervical manipulation, traction or compression testing. Document baseline measures.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why is neck pain not required for the diagnosis? Because the cord can be compressed without much pain. Hand and gait signs are the main clues.
Why avoid traction here? It may change the position of structures around the cord, and benefit is not established. The safer decision is to avoid it until a physician has reviewed the imaging.

The patient has only one positive Hoffmann sign and normal gait. What now? One sign has limited value alone. Complete the UMN screen. If other signs are present, refer. If all others are normal, document and monitor, with a clear plan to re-test.
Why document baseline gait and grip? So that change over time can be recognised and communicated to the physician.
A patient starts to lose bladder control with these signs. What urgency? Emergency. It suggests advanced cord involvement.
**Initial approach:** recognise, document, refer. No neck loading.
**Justifying findings:** UMN signs, hand and gait change.
**Priority:** safe referral at the right urgency.
**Manual therapy:** none to the cervical spine before medical review.
**Exercise:** only after physician guidance.
**Modalities:** not indicated.
**Tell the patient:** you need a medical specialist to check your neck, report sudden changes.
**Avoid:** manipulation, traction, end-range testing.
**Measure:** gait, hand function, reflexes, validated scale.
**If no improvement or worse:** urgent referral.
**Referral triggers:** any UMN signs with clinical change.
**Discharge criteria:** set by the medical team and rehabilitation goals.
**Can be tested:** whether combined clinical signs raise or lower the likelihood of MRI-confirmed compression; whether structured rehabilitation improves function.
**Hypotheses:** that avoiding neck loading before imaging reduces risk. It is a precaution, not a proven effect.
**Future questions:** the best non-surgical rehabilitation for mild myelopathy.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: List the main symptoms of cervical myelopathy.
Perform and interpret Hoffmann, Babinski, clonus and gait tests.
Choose between emergency, urgent and routine action.
Explain why you avoid neck manipulation when myelopathy is suspected.

sections.A: Myelopathy ka matlab hai gardan mein spinal cord par dabao ya chot. Aksar umar ke saath canal tang ho jati hai (disc, hadi ke ubhar, mota ligament). Cord poore jism ke signal le jati hai, is liye haath, taangein, balance aur kabhi peshab par asar hota hai.
sections.B: Haath bhaari ya sunn lagte hain (button lagana, likhna mushkil), chalna ladkhadata ya akda hua hota hai, aur aksar dono haath ya dono taangein mutasir hoti hain. Gardan jhukane par reedh mein current jaisa jhatka (Lhermitte) bhi ho sakta hai.
sections.C: Sawaal haath ke kaam, chalne aur balance, dono taraf ke symptoms, current jaise jhatkon aur peshab-pakhane ki tabdeeli ke baare mein hon. Har jawab cord ki taraf ishara karta hai ya usay rule out karta hai.
sections.D: Chaal dekhein, tandem walk aur Romberg karein, haath ki pakar aur grip-release check karein, chaaron limbs ka poora neuro exam karein, aur Hoffmann, clonus, Babinski jaise UMN signs dekhein.
sections.E: Koi aik test akela faisla nahi karta. Hoffmann, Babinski, clonus aur chaal ke tests ko mila kar dekhein.
sections.F: Radiculopathy, carpal tunnel, peripheral neuropathy, MS aur motor neuron disease isi jaisi lag sakti hain. Farq UMN signs, chaal aur dono taraf ke pattern se pata chalta hai.
sections.G: Tezi se barhti kamzori, haath ya chaal ka bigarna, ya peshab-pakhane ki tabdeeli ke saath naye signs: foran referral. Aise patient par gardan ka koi tez technique nahi.
sections.H: Pehle emergency red flag dekhein. Phir haath ka bhaari-pan, chaal ki tabdeeli ya UMN signs hon to myelopathy ka shak. Tezi se bigar raha ho to usi din, warna chand dinon mein specialist ke paas bhejein, aur findings likh kar dein.
sections.I: Jab tak cord par dabao ka shak hai, gardan par manipulation, traction ya zor wali mobilisation bilkul nahi. Doctor ki ijazat ke baad sirf halka thoracic aur shoulder kaam.
sections.J: Doctor ke assessment se pehle strengthening shuru na karein. Uske baad supervised chaal aur balance training, haath ki mahaarat aur girne se bachao.
sections.K: Machines cord ka dabao kam nahi kartin. Garmi ya electrical cheezein sensation ke bigarne ko chhupa sakti hain, is liye inhein na lagayein.
sections.L: Pehchanein, likhein, sahi urgency se refer karein, aur patient ko samjhayein ke gardan ki imaging zaroori hai aur achanak bigarne par foran bataye.
sections.M: Har visit par chaal, haath ka kaam, taaqat, reflexes aur peshab ka haal check karein. Kisi bhi cheez mein bigar ho to foran refer karein.
sections.N: 63 saal ke aadmi ke dono haath sunn hain, cheezein girti hain, chaal larzti hai aur Hoffmann positive hai. Pehle khud sochein ke kya karna hai, phir jawab dekhein.
sections.chapter-summary-treatment-decision: Mukhtasar: pehchano, likho, refer karo. Doctor ki ijazat se pehle gardan par koi load nahi.
